Container.Name: isputnik-video
Container.Overview:
The video engine for isputnik.home, in a container of its own: TV shows and movies scanned from your video folders, laid out the way Jellyfin and Kodi read them, described from .nfo files and TMDB (posters, backdrops, cast, sets of films, genres), and played in the browser and in the iSputnik TV app. A file a browser plays as it is goes as it is; the rest is converted while it plays, on the CPU or on an Intel CPU's graphics, with HDR tone-mapped and Blu-ray subtitles drawn in. Each person resumes where they stopped, intros and credits are skipped, viewers away from home are held under a quality cap. Everything runs on your server; nothing is sent anywhere.
This is an add-on for isputnik.home and does nothing on its own: it has no sign-in and no pages. Install it beside the isputnik container; video libraries are added, shared and watched in isputnik.home. Set it up from isputnik.home, on Control panel, Settings, Apps, Video. Before installing, press Generate secret there and copy it (it is shown once); paste it into the Gateway Secret field below, which is required. Give the container your video share as Video Folders (read-only: the engine never writes to it). Once it runs, enter its address on the same page (http://[your Unraid IP]:4300 as installed here) and press Test connection, which then says Paired. Then add a library under Control panel, Library, Libraries, Add library, Video. Needs isputnik.home 4.38 or newer.
Container.Changes:
### 2026.11.13 — 0.36.1 Released for real - **0.35.0 and 0.36.0 reach the image at last.** Neither was published: the tests that run before the image is built failed, because the ffmpeg they used (a separate build, not the one the image ships) crashed whenever it put an MPEG-TS video into an MP4, which is how a copy for download is finished. The tests now use the same kind of ffmpeg as the image. This release carries everything in 0.35.0 (converting in memory unless /transcode is a disk, one shared conversion, films kept once converted, Keep ready) and 0.36.0 (big films start sooner). - **A copy for download is put together from one stream.** Its kept pieces are now handed to ffmpeg one after another rather than through a list file: simpler, and nothing left behind if it stops.
### 2026.11.12 — 0.36.0 Big films start sooner - **The first play of a big MKV no longer waits for the whole file to be read.** A film whose picture is sent as it is can only be cut where its keyframes are, and the engine used to find them by reading every byte of the file. On a 30 GB Blu-ray rip on an array disk that took several minutes (longer than the player waited), so the film sat on "Getting it ready…" or failed to start the first time. The keyframes now come from the file's own index, checking each one the way ffmpeg does, since MakeMKV and mkvmerge mark more frames than ffmpeg can cut on: seconds instead of minutes. A file whose index won't do is read as before. - **Keyframes are read ahead.** After each scan and when the engine starts, it reads the keyframes of the titles that will need them, one file at a time and never starting a new one while someone is watching, so even a file that has to be read whole is ready before anyone presses Play.
### 2026.11.12 — 0.35.0 Memory first, one cache, kept ready - **Converted video stays out of the container.** The engine now checks whether `/transcode` is a disk mapped into the container. If it isn't (the Unraid template's Transcode path left empty), video is converted in memory only and no copies for download are prepared there, so nothing fills `docker.img`. With a disk, the admin picks memory only, memory then the disk (the default), or the disk only, and one memory limit is shared by everyone watching (a tenth of the server's memory, at most 1 GB, to start with). isputnik.home 4.88 shows the disk and its free space on Settings › Video › Converting video. Older homes keep working with their memory-per-viewer setting. - **One conversion per version, shared.** Two people watching the same film at the same quality and sound track now share one conversion instead of making it twice, and joining a film someone is already watching takes no place from the household's limit. - **Films kept once converted all the way through.** With a disk, a film whose picture had to be re-encoded is kept once someone has watched it to the end, so it plays next time with nothing converted, also after a restart. A film left at 70% or more is finished off in the background so it is kept too. Kept films and copies for download share one limit (Room for kept video, 50 GB to start with); the ones used longest ago go first. - **Copies for download are made through the same cache.** A copy whose picture is re-encoded is made as the version a viewer would get, a stretch at a time and resumable, then put together into the MP4 in seconds. Copies asked for are carried on after a restart. - **Keep ready.** An admin can keep a film, a show or one season ready at 1080p, 720p or 480p (`/admin/keep-ready`): converted ahead of time in the background and never removed to make room. A show's new episodes follow unless asked not to. - **When downloads are prepared.** The queue runs right away, only when the server is idle, or only between two times at night, with a number of jobs at once and a limit on how many downloads one member may have waiting (`/admin/jobs`). Copies going to someone away from home can be held to a download speed so streaming keeps its share of the upload link.
### 2026.11.11 — 0.34.0 Off the row, and new again - **Take something off Continue watching.** `DELETE /video/api/continue/:id` takes a show (asked by any of its episodes) or a film (every part of it) off the row for the person asking, so isputnik.home 4.86 can offer **Remove from Continue watching** on each card. Nothing is forgotten: the place in it stays, and playing it again, or marking it watched or unwatched, brings it back. Before, a film abandoned halfway or a show nobody meant to go on with stayed on the row for good. - **Every film and show card says when it came** (`addedAt`), so home can keep **Recently added** to the last weeks instead of calling a years-old title new just because nothing came after it. - **A new season makes a show new again.** A show is now dated by the later of when it was first found and when the scan last found an episode it didn't have, so it moves back to the top of Recently added. A file renamed or moved to another folder, with the same season and episode number, doesn't count. Episodes found before this version don't count either: only those the scan finds from now on.
### 2026.11.10 — 0.33.0 Copies prepared for download - **A download optimized for a phone or tablet is now prepared here, on a queue.** isputnik.home 4.82 asks for a smaller copy of a film or episode (480p, 720p or 1080p); the engine makes it as one MP4 and the device fetches the finished file at full speed. Before, the film was converted while the phone waited on the connection, which was slow and loaded the server for as long as the download took. - **Kind to the server.** One copy is made at a time, on the GPU where there is one; without one, at low priority and with half the CPU's cores. A copy being made stands still while anyone is watching converted video, and carries on after. - **Kept for the next person.** A copy made once serves everyone who may see that title. Together they stay under a size set in home's Settings → Video → **Copies for download** (20 GB to start with); past it, the ones used longest ago go. A copy of a file that has changed since is made again. - **Where they are kept:** in a `copies` folder inside `/transcode` when that is mapped, otherwise beside the catalog. Map `/transcode` to a disk with room for them. The conversion folder is still emptied on start, but no longer the copies in it. - A 1080p copy is held to about 2.5 GB for a two-hour film, lower than a 1080p stream; 720p is about 1.4 GB and 480p about 0.7 GB.
Container.Requires: Needs the isputnik (isputnik.home) container, version 4.38 or newer, installed on the same server. The engine is reached only through it.

Config.Name: Engine Port
Config.Description: The port the isputnik container reaches the engine on: enter http://[your Unraid IP]:[this port] as the Video address in isputnik.home (Control panel, Settings, Apps). Not for browsers: video is watched inside isputnik.home. On br0 with a fixed IP, or on a user-defined network shared with the isputnik container, this mapping is not used and the address is the container's own IP or name with port 4300.

Config.Name: Config & Data
Config.Description: Stores the catalog: shows, seasons, episodes and movies found in the video folders, posters and each person's progress (a SQLite database and a picture cache). Keep it apart from the isputnik container's appdata. isputnik.home's backups include a copy of the database.

Config.Name: Video Folders
Config.Description: The share that holds your shows and movies, mounted read-only: the engine never writes to it. Each video library is a folder under it, for example Shows or Movies, chosen in isputnik.home when the library is added.

Config.Name: Transcode
Config.Description: Optional fast disk for video: conversion that overflows memory, and copies prepared for download. Point it at a cache-pool or SSD folder. Left empty, video is converted in memory only and no copies are prepared; how much memory is set in the app (Videos › Settings).

Config.Name: Intel GPU
Config.Description: Optional. /dev/dri to convert video on an Intel CPU's graphics (Quick Sync) instead of the CPU: several viewers at once for little CPU. Leave empty to convert on the CPU. Settings, Video in isputnik.home shows what was found.

Config.Name: Gateway Secret
Config.Description: The secret isputnik.home signs its requests with, so this engine knows who is signed in. Make it first, in isputnik.home on Control panel, Settings, Apps, Video (Generate secret; it is shown once), and paste it here. Required: the engine refuses to start without one, or with one shorter than 32 characters. Everything else about video is managed inside isputnik.home.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the engine runs as. It runs unprivileged (not root); on first start it takes ownership of the Config & Data path as this user. This user must be able to read the Video Folders. 99 (nobody) matches the default owner of an Unraid share.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the engine runs as. 100 (users) matches the default group of an Unraid share.

Config.Name: Log Level
Config.Description: trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal or silent. isputnik.home shows this log and the engine's own event record under Control panel, Overview, Logs.
